producer.summary: Launch press release describes sweet, creamy notes of pipe tobacco, seasoned oak and butterscotch; charcoal mellowed before aging in new toasted and charred barrels. No separate nose/palate/finish given.

critics.nose: Tobacco, leather and toffee, with vanilla and candied strawberry developing in the glass.
critics.palate: Heavily oak-driven and tannic; water softens it to show cherry, cola, tobacco, leather, cinnamon, caraway and clove.
critics.finish: Medium length with a lingering smoky quality.
critics.summary: Prefers it to the 10 Year as extra age tames the sweetness, though the oak can dominate; reviewer's favorite current JD release.

critics.nose: Brown sugar butter, maple-soaked corn cakes, nuttiness, seasoned oak, brown spice and light vanilla.
critics.palate: Buttered grits, maple syrup, cinnamon-led baking spice, velvety oak, vanilla coffee and mashed banana; proof feels restrained.
critics.finish: Mellow with no burn; bruleed banana, caramel and butterscotch with subtle oak.
critics.summary: An easy, effortless drinker, though the reviewer feels the Lincoln County Process limits complexity.

facts.cask: New toasted and charred American white oak; charcoal mellowed before aging

notes: Producer info is the combined descriptor from the 2023 launch press release; jackdaniels.com product page returned 404.

producer.nose: Vanilla bean, Earl Grey tea, caramel and sweet tobacco.
producer.palate: Pecan pie, whole grain toast and grapefruit peel.
producer.finish: Nutmeg, birch beer and dry oak tannin.
producer.summary: Hyper-small-batch 13-year bourbon, non-chill filtered and proofed with Rosendale Mines limestone water.

critics.nose: Candied apple, cinnamon, nutmeg, clove and leather.
critics.palate: Tart red apple, vanilla, caramel, espresso, toasted oak and bitter chocolate.
critics.finish: Warm and spicy.
critics.summary: Fall 2021 small-batch release at 93 proof; profiled as spicy and rich.

notes: Input lists 101 proof but producer page and Distiller list 93 proof; the Kansas label may be a different batch strength, so notes may not match exactly. Skipped Paste's 2020 review (earlier single-barrel, variable-proof version).

critics.nose: Port influence brings raisin and mint forward, with more clove than the unfinished bourbon.
critics.palate: Apple butter gives a rich mouthfeel; baking spice throughout.
critics.finish: Sweet with lingering baking spice; possibly too sweet for some drinkers.
critics.summary: Graded A- (letter grade). Reviewed at 90 proof, finished in 14-year-old ruby port casks.

critics.palate: Butterscotch, clove and banana bread.
critics.finish: Gentle fruity port notes add complexity without overwhelming the bourbon.
critics.summary: An appealing pairing of spicy bourbon and sweeter port character.

facts.cask: Finished in 14-year-old ruby port wine casks

notes: Producer site unreachable (403/DNS); no producer notes. Facts from Drinkhacker (MGP sourcing is the reviewer's presumption). Input had no proof; 90 proof per Drinkhacker/Distiller.

producer.nose: Freshly brewed coffee and rich molasses with subtle sweet corn and spice.
producer.palate: Layered vanilla and young oak blending into milk chocolate.
producer.finish: Medium-long and balanced; oak and vanilla with a touch of dark roast coffee and brown spice.
producer.summary: Master blender Alan Kennedy's notes as relayed in launch press coverage (Northwest Beer Guide), not fetched from the brand site. Color described as deep amber.

facts.mash_bill: Corn, rye and barley (proportions not given); charcoal mellowed (Lincoln County Process)
facts.cask: Cold-steeped, custom-roasted Honduran Arabica coffee beans (Agalta region) introduced during final maturation

notes: 2025 coffee-infused release, sold as a bourbon flavored with coffee. No independent critic review fetched (Whiskey Apostle review timed out).

producer.nose: Toffee, honey and black walnut moving toward chocolate and caramel, with cherry, mint and strong rye spice (nose and palate described together).
producer.palate: Same combined description as nose: toffee, honey, black walnut, chocolate, caramel, cherry, mint and rye spice.
producer.finish: Oak and toastiness lead, lingering with warm gingerbread.
producer.summary: 2026 edition notes from michters.com; fully matured US*1 rye re-barreled in a custom toasted barrel of 24-month air-dried wood, bottled at barrel strength.

critics.nose: Black cherry and walnut like a fruit cobbler, then brown sugar, honey, molasses, toffee and taffy.
critics.palate: Toasted honey, pecan, semi-sweet chocolate, Derby-pie character, blackstrap molasses, then oak; apple pie spice for balance.
critics.finish: Hot and drying with oak, cinnamon gum and black pepper.
critics.summary: Wood-forward and possibly divisive but well made; good with dessert. 2023 release, sampled at 109.4 proof.

facts.cask: Finished in custom toasted (not charred) barrel from 24-month air-dried wood

notes: Barrel-strength proof varies by barrel/year; producer page is 2026 edition (avg 109.1), VinePair is 2023 edition, input label 108 proof. Producer notes combine nose and palate.

producer.nose: Oak, vanilla, sweet cream and fruitcake shifting to cinnamon, spice and florals.
producer.palate: Cherry, raisin and dark honey giving way to herbal clove, spearmint and thyme.
producer.finish: Long, with spice, mature oak, char and pepper.
producer.summary: Official 2024 Camp Nelson B release notes as relayed by Breaking Bourbon's press-release page; sixth-floor barrels, non-chill filtered, barrel proof, highest-proof Russell's Reserve to date.

critics.nose: Sweet oak, molasses and honeyed cornbread, nutmeg and boozy cherries, then spearmint and cocoa.
critics.palate: Syrupy honey, dark oak and tannin, brown butter, dark fruits (blackcurrant, prune, fig, cherry), chocolate and creamy peanut butter.
critics.finish: Long and oaky with cherry-cola notes; water brings out black cherry, dark grape and a brandy-like quality.
critics.summary: Reviewer's favorite of the three Single Rickhouse releases, narrowly ahead of Camp Nelson F.

critics.nose: Ethanol up front; with time, warm honey and golden raisins.
critics.palate: Apple, raisin, honey and lemon with crisp oak and restrained spice.
critics.finish: Long and warming with spice, oak, char and pepper, not overly dry.
critics.summary: Nothing to dislike except the steep price; rated 'Bar' on the site's buy/bar/bust scale.

facts.region: Kentucky (Camp Nelson B rickhouse, sixth floor)

notes: Identified via 120.2 proof as the 2024 Camp Nelson B edition. Producer notes are relayed via Breaking Bourbon press release.

producer.palate: Citrus, burnt sugar, cinnamon, caramel and lemon zest.
producer.finish: Bourbon spice balanced against the Sauternes cask influence.
producer.summary: Producer notes as relayed by retailer Caskers (not fetched from jeffersonsbourbon.com, which returned 404). Finished in forty Chateau Suduiraut barrels in a 'hot box' warehouse.

facts.cask: New charred American oak, then several months in ex-Chateau Suduiraut Sauternes French oak casks in a heated 'hot box' warehouse; 40 barrels

notes: Label spelling 'Suduirait' is Chateau Suduiraut. No critic review obtained (Whiskey Were Here hit a redirect loop; Distiller has only a community rating).

critics.nose: Juniper-led with bright lime zest and hints of red grapefruit.
critics.palate: Bitter orange and lemon, then angelica and pink grapefruit, closing on creamy licorice root and piney juniper.
critics.finish: Long, moderately warm, with citrus zest and earthy undertones.
critics.summary: Highly recommended classic-style gin; suggested for martinis, Tom Collins, Corpse Reviver #2 and G&Ts.

critics.nose: Bold juniper and soft citrus: grapefruit, blood orange and finger lime with licorice candy and angelica.
critics.palate: Creamy and full-bodied with chamomile florals and dominant grapefruit; rich yet bright, earthy base.
critics.finish: Clean, licorice-led, with a spicy tingle.
critics.summary: Called outstanding: powerful yet structured, bolder and more citrus-forward than standard Tanqueray. Reviewed at 47.3%.

facts.mash_bill: Wheat base spirit; botanicals juniper, coriander, licorice, angelica, chamomile plus fresh whole lime, orange and grapefruit (citrus distilled separately)
facts.cask: Distilled in the small 'Tiny Ten' still (about 500 L per batch); unaged

notes: Tanqueray producer page 404'd; no producer notes. Facts from The Gin is In (Tiny Ten batch size from 88 Bamboo). ABV 47.3% per 88 Bamboo.

producer.summary: Producer copy relayed on the Whisky Advocate store product page: rich, smooth and earthy with notable complexity; sweet orange in a blend with no bitter botanicals; green cardamom adds spicy, sweet floral notes. No nose/palate/finish split.

critics.nose: Classically juniper-forward with green pine, orange zest and a distinctive camphor note.
critics.palate: Bright, green pine moving to citrus and spice; vanilla custard with lemon and sweet orange, then cardamom, white pepper and cassia.
critics.finish: Long, with licorice root and nuttiness, moderate warmth, slight astringency and light sweetness.
critics.summary: A versatile classic for martinis, Negronis and Last Words; complex despite a short botanical list. Reviewed at 41.2%.

critics.palate: Less crisp than typical London Dry, earthier from heavier root botanicals, with smoother juniper.
critics.finish: Unusually long for a gin, dominated by licorice and angelica.
critics.summary: A distinctive, heritage-driven gin set apart from modern London Dry conventions.

facts.mash_bill: Grain spirit base; seven botanicals: juniper, coriander seed, orange peel, lemon peel, green cardamom, orris root, angelica root
facts.cask: One-shot distillation in a 160+ year-old still with short neck and sharply bent lye pipe; unaged

notes: Producer site 404'd; producer copy is retailer-relayed and summary-only.

producer.summary: Trade sheet calls it a 'meadow in bloom': a balanced gin of 19 botanicals with herbaceous character, bright citrus and delicate florals, versatile in cocktails.

critics.nose: Balanced layers of soft juniper, pine resin, fennel, lime zest, pepper and baking spice.
critics.palate: Juniper berry moving into dry green herbs (cilantro, dill) with earthy dark licorice.
critics.finish: Long pine, mint and ginger with lemony hops, candied orange and lime.
critics.summary: Graded A (letter grade); the most classic-leaning gin in St. George's range, versatile and great in martinis. Reviewed at 90 proof.

critics.nose: Orange, cinnamon and cardamom over a heady bay leaf note; spicy, herbal and citrusy.
critics.palate: Cinnamon stick, ginger candy and bright pepper with a thick warm texture; aquavit-like caraway, then juniper and hops.
critics.finish: Warm and spicy with a cool licorice-like back note.
critics.summary: Highly recommended contemporary gin where juniper supports the 19 botanicals; classic gin fans may want more juniper.

notes: Producer product page 404'd; producer info from trade-support PDF (summary only).

producer.nose: Ripe, juicy grape with meadow flowers, acacia blossom and a touch of cedar.
producer.summary: Producer notes as relayed by retailer Cognac-Expert.com. Revives an 1840 cognac formula using Angeac eaux-de-vie; VS-grade Grande Champagne.

critics.nose: Wood spice suggesting fresh-sanded oak and sandalwood, with cinnamon, butterscotch, honey and citrus zest.
critics.palate: Sweet grape and honeyed oak spice building to white pepper; butterscotch into marmalade, cinnamon and nuts.
critics.finish: Green grape, honey and butterscotch, then lingering wood spice, pepper, cinnamon and a hint of mint.
critics.summary: Works both neat and in cocktails; fulfils the brief of reviving historic cocktail cognac. Reviewed at 45%.

critics.nose: Ripe pear, wax, green grape and delicate florals.
critics.palate: Mint and crushed peanut on a creamy texture.
critics.summary: Fruity, floral and higher-proof than most VS cognacs; designed mainly for mixing.

facts.mash_bill: Grande Champagne cru; distilled in Charentais alembic

notes: Producer notes are retailer-relayed (Cognac-Expert). Developed 2011 with David Wondrich per Distiller.

critics.nose: Complex bouquet of raw honey, vanilla sugar and rich caramel.
critics.palate: Round, well-balanced mouthfeel with great complexity.
critics.finish: Mellow and lightly smoky.
critics.summary: Highly complex, balanced old Grande Champagne blend.

critics.nose: Mild wood with mineral-water freshness, lime, vanilla and blanched almond, developing mint.
critics.palate: Smooth then fiery mid-palate; dried fruit, bitter walnut, dark chocolate, preserved cherry, truffle and mushroom, florals.
critics.finish: Wood takes over: elegant but drying with pepper, spice, tobacco and lingering rancio.
critics.summary: Five-star review emphasizing classic rancio character (earthy, bitter-nut, oily, eucalyptus). Reviewed at 40%.

facts.age: NAS; blend of 50+ eaux-de-vie described as very old (Malt Mileage cites 50-60 years)
facts.cask: French oak (Troncais oak per Malt Mileage)

notes: Hine producer page rendered empty (JS) so no producer notes. Age of components varies by source; treat as approximate.

producer.nose: Subtle vanilla opening to rose and violet florals, plum and apricot, then sweet apple and pear pastry.
producer.summary: Producer notes as relayed by The Whisky Exchange retailer page; amber to golden color.

critics.nose: Fresh floral and citrus notes with green grape, vanilla, herbs and sandalwood.
critics.palate: Light oak and fresh green grape give a crisp feel, with vanilla, cinnamon, ginger and citrus.
critics.finish: Smooth and crisp with butterscotch, green grape, lemongrass and gooseberry.
critics.summary: Recommended for sipping and quality mixing. Reviewed at 40%; originally 2014, revised 2018.

facts.age: NAS; blended to represent about 10 years old (per Rum Howler)
facts.mash_bill: Ugni Blanc and Colombard grapes; Grande Champagne 1er cru

notes: Producer notes are retailer-relayed (The Whisky Exchange); Rum Howler notes caramel coloring.

critics.nose: Toasty oak with cherry, banana, coconut, vanilla and clove.
critics.palate: Burnt sugar against dry oak tannin; blackened fruitcake, cinnamon and clove.
critics.finish: Long, spiced creme brulee.
critics.summary: Warming and festive: burnt sugar and caramel with Christmas spice and a hint of Jamaican fruit. Sampled July 2021 at 40%.

critics.nose: Subtle cherry, vanilla and clove; second taster found coconut, pineapple and banana.
critics.palate: Smooth with apricot, vanilla and cinnamon; butterscotch and coconut.
critics.finish: Some cinnamon but very short and not warming.
critics.summary: Drinks lighter than most dark rums and lacks wood complexity, yet a pleasant sipper. Earlier Plantation-branded bottling; ABV not stated in review.

critics.nose: Molasses, black pepper and a green note; fruity high tones with heavy esters and cinnamon.
critics.palate: Weighty and full-bodied with savory notes and spice cake.
critics.finish: Cooked caramel, tropical fruit and brown butter.
critics.summary: Retailer staff note praising it as complex value for cocktails or neat sipping (Planteray-branded bottling).

facts.mash_bill: Blend of younger Caribbean rum with long-aged Jamaican pot still rum; component islands differ by source and over time (Barbados or Trinidad)
facts.cask: Charred American oak, then French oak (Cognac) casks, married in vats
facts.region: Caribbean, blended/bottled by Maison Ferrand, France

notes: Planteray is the renamed Plantation brand; producer site unreachable. Sources disagree on blend composition (Difford's: Barbados + 10-15 yr Jamaican; All At Sea: Trinidad + Jamaican; Astor: Barbados/Trinidad aging). Difford's notes 15 g/L sugar. All At Sea review predates rename.

producer.nose: Fruit-forward with dried apricot, fresh peach and a hint of molasses.
producer.finish: Rich and mildly sweet with brief citrus and nutty notes.
producer.summary: Official Appleton Estate notes; harvest gold/amber color, blended by Joy Spence with no added flavors.

critics.nose: Mild and fruity: tobacco, orange zest, ripe banana, apricot, liquorice, black tea, biscuit, red apple, toffee and vanilla.
critics.palate: Woody with tobacco, nutmeg, nuts and marmalade, plus banana, pear, black pepper, caramel and raisin; somewhat thin body.
critics.finish: Short to medium with tropical and dried fruit.
critics.summary: Called underrated: complex and balanced for its light body; recommended in daiquiris. Reviewed at 40%.

critics.nose: Guava, pineapple and passion fruit against brown sugar, molasses, vanilla and caramel.
critics.palate: Sweet and slightly saline like salted caramel with oak and light dry tannin; velvety.
critics.finish: Dry, with lingering salted caramel, molasses and oak.
critics.summary: Smooth, flavorful and versatile in cocktails, especially eggnog. Reviewed as 'Signature Blend' at 40%.

facts.mash_bill: Blend of pot still and column still rums (Difford's: 15 aged rums)

notes: Now sold as 'Appleton Estate Signature' (formerly Signature Blend). 15-rum blend figure from Difford's Guide listing.

critics.nose: Woody and slightly herbal: cardamom, cocoa biscuit, cassia and fennel seed with red apple, sour cherry and unripe peach.
critics.palate: Sweeter than the nose suggests; coconut-chocolate, biscuit, honey, allspice, peach, mango and vanilla.
critics.finish: Medium, with dried fruit and charred oak.
critics.summary: A step up from the 5 Year; rounded with appealing dried fruit and spice. Reviewed at 40%.

critics.nose: Light, fruity Bajan style with summer fruits, vanilla and bourbon-cask spice.
critics.palate: Oak, spicy bourbon notes, grape, coconut, caramel sweetness and a touch of toffee.
critics.summary: A really good rum though fairly ordinary next to other recent Foursquare releases. Reviewed at 40%.

critics.nose: Vanilla, play-dough, caramel, saltwater taffy and fresh croissant.
critics.palate: Caramel, vanilla, saltwater taffy, orange peel and molasses.
critics.finish: Medium, tannic and a bit thin, with oak and citrus.
critics.summary: Classic, additive-free Bajan rum best as an affordable mixer or casual sipper. Reviewed at 40%.

facts.mash_bill: Molasses-based blend of pot and column still rum (Foursquare)

notes: Input label lists 43% ABV (86 proof) but all reviews fetched are of the 40% bottling; facts reflect the 40% reviews. No producer notes found. Rum Barrel says no added sweeteners; Fat Rum Pirate suspects caramel coloring.
